questions.q: State the two fundamental properties of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle that are used to solve length and angle problems.
questions.a: The two properties are: (1) The lengths of the two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal. (2) The tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact. A wrong answer (e.g., mentioning only one property or confusing with secant properties) reveals the student cannot recall the foundational theorems needed to set up equations in word problems.

questions.q: In a circle with centre O, tangents PA and PB are drawn from external point P. If ∠APB = 70°, find ∠AOB. Explain why the quadrilateral OAPB has two right angles.
questions.a: ∠AOB = 110°. Quadrilateral OAPB has ∠OAP = ∠OBP = 90° because radius is perpendicular to tangent. Sum of angles in quadrilateral = 360°, so ∠AOB = 360° - 90° - 90° - 70° = 110°. A wrong answer (e.g., ∠AOB = 70°) shows the student does not understand the angle sum property of quadrilaterals or the perpendicular property, leading to incorrect angle calculations in word problems.

questions.q: From a point P outside a circle of radius 6 cm, two tangents PA and PB are drawn such that PA = 8 cm. Find the distance OP from the external point to the centre.
questions.a: In right triangle OAP, OA = 6 cm (radius), AP = 8 cm (tangent length). By Pythagoras, OP² = OA² + AP² = 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100. So OP = 10 cm. A wrong answer (e.g., OP = 14 cm by adding 6+8) reveals the student fails to recognize the right triangle formed by radius and tangent, a critical misconception for all tangent length problems.

questions.q: Two circles of radii 5 cm and 3 cm touch externally. A common external tangent touches the larger circle at A and the smaller at B. The centres are O and O'. If the distance between centres is 8 cm, find the length of the tangent segment AB. (Hint: Draw perpendiculars from centres to the tangent.)
questions.a: Draw OO' = 8 cm. Drop perpendiculars OA ⟂ AB (OA = 5) and O'B ⟂ AB (O'B = 3). Construct rectangle O'AXO where X is on OA. Then OX = OA - O'B = 5 - 3 = 2 cm. In right triangle OO'X, O'X = AB. By Pythagoras, AB² = OO'² - OX² = 8² - 2² = 64 - 4 = 60. So AB = √60 = 2√15 cm. A wrong answer (e.g., AB = 8 cm) shows the student cannot decompose the figure into a rectangle and right triangle, a key spatial reasoning skill for multi-circle tangent problems.

questions.q: A student solves the problem: "From point P, tangents PA and PB are drawn to a circle with centre O. If OP = 13 cm and radius = 5 cm, find the perimeter of quadrilateral OAPB." The student writes: Perimeter = OA + AP + PB + BO = 5 + 12 + 12 + 5 = 34 cm. Is this correct? Justify.
questions.a: Yes, correct. In right triangle OAP, OA = 5, OP = 13, so AP = √(13² - 5²) = 12 cm. Since PA = PB = 12 cm, perimeter = 5 + 12 + 12 + 5 = 34 cm. If a student says "incorrect" or calculates AP incorrectly (e.g., using 13+5), it reveals they cannot verify a solution or they misunderstand the Pythagorean relationship, which is essential for checking answers in board exams.

questions.q: Create a word problem involving a circle, two tangents from an external point, and a given angle between the tangents. The problem should ask for the radius of the circle given the distance from the external point to the centre. Provide the solution.
questions.a: Example problem: "From a point P, 17 cm away from the centre O of a circle, two tangents PA and PB are drawn. If the angle between the tangents is 60°, find the radius of the circle." Solution: In right triangle OAP, ∠APO = 30° (since OP bisects ∠APB). sin 30° = OA/OP => 1/2 = r/17 => r = 8.5 cm. A poor problem (e.g., missing data, inconsistent numbers) shows the student cannot synthesize the properties into a coherent problem, indicating shallow understanding of the interdependence of length and angle properties.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: This node covers the application of tangent properties — specifically the equality of tangent lengths from an external point and the ______ of the tangent to the radius at the point of contact — to solve multi-step word problems involving unknown lengths and angles in geometric configurations with circles.
Fill in the blank: Two ______ paths from a gate outside the garden just touch the garden boundary at points A and B.
Fill in the blank: Imagine a circular garden with a radius of ______ metres.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can independently translate a word problem into a labeled diagram, identify which tangent properties apply, set up equations using equal tangent lengths and right angles, solve for unknown lengths or angles, and verify the solution satisfies all geometric constraints.
